chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: Meeting Olin Dewalt over a game of marbles
summary: Gus meets Olin Dewalt, whose father owned the Lincoln Theatre, while watching a marbles game; Olin takes him in free and his mother approves.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, in Houston, while I was in grade school, --
-- well, I met a friend, his father owned a theatre there.
The Lincoln Theatre in Houston, Texas. Used to be -- it was on Prairie.
And after I got out of high school, I hate to jump like this, but --
But I was going to Booker Washington,
and so I was in football and stuff like that in high school. But I would always go to the theatre, that's the reason why I just -- around like this, to let you know.
Yeah, yeah. 'Cause Being his friend, you could -- well, what would you do, go backstage?
Well, no. I was going to the theatre, and they had -- they was showing movies.
And once in a while, they would have a special show on, or something like that.
But they always had a pit bands, see.
Well, this Sunday, after I came from church, and I passed by Olin's house -- his name was Olin Dewalt.

Dewalt. Well, they owned the theatre, see. I didn't know that. He was out in his yard, shooting marbles with his cousin, see. And it was during the winter-time, and it was kind of cold, see. And I stopped to look at

them shoot marbles. He missed, and so I said, "You can't shoot marbles worth nothing," and it made him angry. He said, "Well, you're so smart, you got on in and show me what you can do," and like that.

So my hands were warm because I had them in my pocket. So I hit the marbles and I was doing real good until my hands got cold, then I missed, see. And then he laughed at me about that. That's the way we met.

And he said, "Where you going?" And I said, "I'm going to the theatre." He said, "Well, come on, wait on me, my daddy owns the theatre and you can go in free with me." I said, "Really?" He says, "Yeah."
That's right. And he carried me in the house and introduced me to his mother. And he was the only son.
But he had two cousins, that lived there also. They were two girls, and one was named Carolyn and the youngest was named Lupe. They were mixed with French and Spanish.
So, okay, I went in and met the family and everything. And my mother always kept me looking good all the time.
That's why I don't understand the kids now.
No, yeah, yeah. They just look tacky in a way.
Yeah. I always looked good, even when I was a kid.
